transcript.text: t/d keeps cutting out after 10 mins then starts again if i leave it. vent hose goes out the window. pls help

The usual reason is restricted airflow—fluff in the filter or a vent hose that is long, crushed, kinked or partly blocked—even if it does reach a window. With it switched off and unplugged, clean the door fluff filter thoroughly and check the entire hose for kinks, squashing and lint; keep the hose as short and straight as practical, with the window end open to the air. If it still cuts out after those checks, a thermostat/thermal cut-out or motor fault becomes more likely and it will need an appliance engineer rather than repeated use.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
ok will check. the cabinet gets really hot before it stops tho. its a small kitchen, hose is behind the dryer

A warm cabinet can be normal on a vented dryer, but becoming really hot and then stopping is not—this sounds like its overheat protection is cutting in and resetting once it cools. The hose being trapped behind it makes restricted airflow the leading cause, especially in a small kitchen. With it switched off and unplugged, pull it forward carefully and make sure the hose has a clear, short run with no flattening, tight bends or fluff at the window end; leave some space behind the dryer rather than pushing it back onto the hose. Do not keep running it while it is overheating. If the hose and filter are clear but it still stops after about ten minutes, the next likely causes are an internal blockage/blower problem or a thermostat/thermal cut-out, which needs an engineer.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
pulled it out, hose is totally crushed behind it and theres fluff in the folds. what now?

That crushed, fluff-filled hose is very likely the cause: it prevents hot air escaping, so the dryer’s overheat protection stops it and then resets as it cools. With the dryer unplugged, take the hose off and remove the fluff all the way through it and from the window end; replace the hose if it is split, badly flattened or cannot be cleared properly. Clean the door filter as well, then refit the hose with a short, free run and leave enough space behind the dryer so it cannot be trapped again. Run one normal load while staying nearby. If it still stops after about ten minutes with a clear, uncrushed vent, stop using it and arrange an engineer to check for an internal lint blockage, blower problem or thermostat/thermal cut-out fault.
[Safety panel] Overheating can be a fire risk. Clean the lint filter and make sure the airflow/vent isn't blocked, and don't leave the dryer running unattended. If it smells of burning, stop using it and unplug it.
